import pandas as pd

# File paths for the source CSV files
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_66/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_66/training_1.csv"

# Load Source 0: School info table
# Index column is the first column (School ID), so we ignore it by index_col=0
df_source0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)

# Load Source 1: Student scores table
# Index column is the first column (Student ID), so we ignore it by index_col=0
df_source1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Transformation plan:
# Target schema: ['school_name': string, 'reading_score': float]
# Source0 has school_name but no reading_score
# Source1 has school_name and reading_score per student
# We want average reading_score per school_name to match target examples (which are aggregated scores per school)
# So we aggregate Source1 by school_name to get average reading_score
# Then join with Source0 on school_name to ensure all schools from Source0 are included (if needed)
# But target examples only show school_name and reading_score, so we only need school_name and average reading_score
# Since Source1 has all reading scores per student, we can just group by school_name and average reading_score
# We do not need Source0 columns except to ensure school_name consistency, but since Source1 already has school_name, we can rely on Source1 aggregation alone.
# However, to follow the instruction "ALL source tables have to be used", we will do an inner join on school_name between Source0 and aggregated Source1.
# This ensures only schools present in Source0 and Source1 are included.
# Finally, select columns as per target schema and write to CSV.

# Aggregate Source1 by school_name to get average reading_score
df_agg_scores = df_source1.groupby('school_name', as_index=False)['reading_score'].mean()

# Join aggregated scores with Source0 on school_name (inner join to keep only schools present in both)
df_joined = pd.merge(df_source0[['school_name']], df_agg_scores, on='school_name', how='inner')

# Ensure column order and types as per target schema
df_result = df_joined[['school_name', 'reading_score']].copy()
df_result['school_name'] = df_result['school_name'].astype(str)
df_result['reading_score'] = df_result['reading_score'].astype(float)

# Write the result to the target CSV file
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_66/target_multisource_cot.csv"
df_result.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_66/training_1.csv", index_col=0)

# Group by school_name and aggregate mean of reading_score
